subject: Hybrid Dedicated Sizing — GPU flavor, TPS & concurrency clarifications
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: dedicated sizing follow-ups & next steps

Hi Asha — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and a handful of clarifying questions so we can size a recommended Dedicated pool and propose a hybrid fallback plan: 

Call recap (short)
- Primary need: low-latency inference for customer-facing search and completions across web + mobile.
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~380 tps (inbound requests). Peak bursts up to ~1,200 tps for short windows.
- Token profile: average request has ~80 prompt tokens and ~60 generation tokens, but some long-context flows hit 1,500 prompt tokens.
- Current preference: Dedicated reserved pool, with Hosted fallbacks during bursts. Also evaluating Private VPC for data controls.

Clarifying asks (so we can recommend GPU flavors & concurrency):
1) Can you confirm what you mean by tps: requests/sec or tokens/sec? From our discussion it sounded like requests/sec—confirm please.
2) For the long-context flows, are those rare (1–2% of requests) or per-session for certain customers?
3) Any hard p95 latency targets (generation-only) we should assume for sizing? You mentioned ~1200ms for web interactions.
4) Are you open to H100 for latency-sensitive routes and A100 (or L4s) for cheaper background routes?

Next steps I propose:
- Please upload the capacity worksheet I attached (edge-capacity-worksheet.xlsx) with 1 week of sample traffic and token mix. That will let our capacity model show GPU count by flavor.
- Ops sync: Neha can run a quick throughput estimate based on your token mix and expected p95.
- If you want, we can schedule a short follow-up (30 min) this week to walk the worksheet and fallback policies.

Attaching: edge-capacity-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet), example-token-mix.csv (sample CSV).

Thanks — Dylan
Dylan Brooks

Subject: Re: Post-call: dedicated sizing follow-ups & next steps

Thanks Dylan — quick answers inline.

1) By tps we meant requests/sec (we track at request level).
2) Long-context flows: about 3% of total requests, concentrated on enterprise customers doing multi-doc summaries. Not per-session — intermittent but predictable windows (end of day reports).
3) p95 target: 900ms end-to-end for web search flows; for multi-doc summaries we're okay with 2.5–3s occasionally.
4) Open to heterogeneous GPU mix: prefer H100 for latency-critical search; A100 for summaries if cost-effective. Would like you to show cost / latency tradeoffs.

I uploaded a sanitized traffic sample to the Drive link you provided (row counts and token columns). Procurement looped in for contract questions.

Asha Rao
Head of Product Operations, Edge Commerce
asha@edgecommerce.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: dedicated sizing follow-ups & next steps

Great, thanks for the clarifications Asha. I pulled the Drive sample and ran a quick back-of-envelope using our throughput model — high level:

- With H100 (pinned to latency routes) and an A100 pool for background jobs, we estimate:
  • H100 pool: 4 nodes (8 GPUs) sizing to handle steady-state ~180 requests/sec of the latency-sensitive route with p95 ~700–900ms depending on batching window and generation length.
  • A100 pool: 6 nodes (12 GPUs) to absorb summary workloads and burst spillover; this covers ~200 rps with average 140 tokens/req.
- Hybrid routing: smart routing rules to pin high-priority routes to H100 and overflow to A100 + Hosted.
- For your peak bursts (1,200 rps) we expect to rely on auto-burst to Hosted API or short-lived pre-warmed Dedicated burst capacity. If you want 100% on Dedicated during peaks, add ~10–12 extra GPUs (A100/H100 mix) — higher cost.

Notes / assumptions:
- Tokenization: we used the token mix in the CSV; if enterprise docs are larger we may need to reserve extra KV cache memory per GPU.
- Quantization: running smaller models with int8 can reduce GPU RAM pressure but increases latency variance — not recommended for p95 < 1s.
- Networking: if you move forward with a VPC/private deployment, we’ll validate MTU and cross-AZ bandwidth; that can affect cold-start for KV cache loads.

Action items:
- Dylan: propose 30-min ops deep-dive Thursday 10:00–10:30 PT?
- Asha: confirm whether Edge Commerce wants to target 100% Dedicated during daily peaks or accept Hosted fallback for bursts.
- I’ll produce a short cost/latency matrix for H100 vs A100 vs mixed pool and share in <48h.

-Neha
